goal: Understand Python memory growth and choose a diagnostic for allocation changes.

initial.text: Python memory research workbench. Review one source at a time and distinguish background information from a diagnostic for allocation changes.

distinct-1.text: Python memory background: reference counting is supplemented by an optional cycle collector. This excerpt contains no allocation comparison or diagnostic steps.

distinct-2.text: Python memory configuration: automatic garbage collection can be enabled or disabled. This excerpt does not identify which code allocated growing memory.

distinct-3.text: Python memory debugging: GC debug flags can retain collected objects for inspection. This excerpt does not provide a before-and-after allocation trace.

suppressed-1.text: Python memory diagnostic: tracemalloc can compare two allocation snapshots and report differences by source line. Start tracing before the workload whose allocation changes you want to investigate.

suppressed-2.text: Python memory investigation: take an allocation snapshot before a workload, take another afterwards, and compare the snapshots to locate allocation growth.

paused-1.text: Python memory context: a garbage collection count is not itself a traceback identifying the source of newly allocated blocks. This observation offers no trace.

paused-2.text: Python memory evidence: tracemalloc statistics can group allocated blocks by filename and line number. Inspect those source locations when investigating growth.

paused-3.text: Python memory retention experiment: a test log records that diagnostic output was not saved. No measured allocation result is available in this controlled record.

probe-1.text: Python memory allocation changes can be examined with snapshot2.compare_to(snapshot1, 'lineno'). The returned statistics describe differences between the recorded allocations, with their source locations.

restored-1.text: Python memory tracing should begin early to capture allocations of interest. A diagnostic plan can compare a baseline snapshot with a post-workload snapshot.

stale-grant.text: Python memory source permissions expired after a backend restart. This is a controlled consent test, not a new allocation measurement.

post-restart.text: Python memory investigation continues with the saved plan: review allocation differences and their source tracebacks, retaining the original observation date.

bad-hash.text: Python memory test: this reviewed excerpt must not be accepted with a different fingerprint. No diagnostic inference is authorised by a mismatched hash.

budget-check.text: Python memory comparison: the next useful step is to inspect before-and-after allocation statistics, but this test deliberately exhausts the model budget.

irrelevant.text: An astronomy reading list describes distant galaxies and telescope schedules. It contains no programming diagnostic or allocation information.
